summary: This article surveys funding options for local entrepreneurs, drawing on a September 15, 2023 Local Economy and Market conference and interviews with founders, a banker and an advisor. It covers traditional loans, alternative lending, crowdfunding, angel investors and VCs, grants, creative financing and pitching. It concludes that funding should fit a long-term plan and is as much about relationships and fit as about money.
one_line: A 2023 local-economy feature on funding routes for entrepreneurs, from bank loans and crowdfunding to VC, grants and pitching, with founder anecdotes.
key_facts: The Local Economy and Market conference took place on September 15, 2023, drawing entrepreneurs to network and explore funding.
Douglas Freeman, founder of Freeman Tech Solutions, said he bootstrapped until it hurt before realizing he needed external funding; he spoke at a workshop on September 22, 2023.

Maria Gonzalez, VP at Local Community Bank, said in an October 3, 2023 interview that banks look for clients with potential for longevity and success, and that lending is about trust, not just numbers.
Traditional bank and credit union loans depend on credit scores, collateral and a convincing business plan, and their high entry barriers and stringent terms can be stifling.
Alternative lenders offer lines of credit, merchant cash advances and microloans, typically at higher interest rates but with flexibility and speed.
Emily Cho, CEO of Cho's Chocolaterie, used an alternative lender so she did not have to put up her house as collateral.
Alternative lending boomed after the 2008 financial crisis and had become a mainstay of entrepreneurial finance by 2023.
Samir Patel's eco-friendly apparel line went viral after a successful crowdfunding campaign in late September 2023; he said it validated the product and made each backer an advocate.
Angel investors usually invest at early stages in exchange for equity, while VCs come in later with larger sums and often more say in running the business.
Lydia Zhang secured VC funding for her AI startup in November 2023 and said maintaining her vision and culture matters as much as the capital.
Grants are money that need not be repaid but are competitive and tied to specific industries or initiatives; Antonio Morales won one for his sustainable farming startup.
Petra Ivanov, a game developer, leveraged her proprietary technology to secure funding and strategic partnerships.
Ryan Jenkins won over investors at a December 1, 2023 pitch event for his health tech startup, advising 'Know your worth, know your business, and know your audience.'
The author has nearly three decades of experience reporting on local economies.
